clue.text: Ball is found after match

indicators.note: the word is is placed after the match word in the answer

parts.note: a test is a match, as in a Test match at cricket

explanation.surface: A ball turns up once the game is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Ball here is the anatomical sense, not a sporting one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ball is a slang word for one of the male reproductive glands.

clue.text: See 19
See 19
Iranian city is cooler with a hot interior

indicators.note: with a hot interior means the a and hot letters go inside the cooler word

parts.note: a fan is something that cools you down
H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An Iranian city has a fan inside that is hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Isfahan is a historic city in central Iran, famed for its mosques.

clue.text: Plant G higher then?

parts.note: if G is the higher note, then F is the lower one, so the letter F sits beside the word lower

explanation.surface: A gardener asks about raising a plant labelled G.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'G higher' as a statement about the alphabet or scale: G is above F, so F is lower, giving F followed by LOWER. Commenters thought the logic loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower is a blooming plant, the kind grown in a garden bed.

clue.text: Place to host up-and-coming little play

indicators.note: to host is to hold another piece inside, as a host holds guests

parts.note: to lay something is to place it down

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A venue hosts a promising little stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up-and-coming little' reads like a description of a young actor, but it is a reversal; 'play' is the slack sense, not a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Play means room to move or freedom, the slack in a rope or a timetable.

clue.text: Cook in wok with odd bits of louse and last of yeast extract

indicators.note: to cook the books is to rework them, so these letters are rearranged
the first, third and fifth letters of louse are taken
only the final letter of yeast is taken

explanation.surface: A recipe for stir-frying lice with a yeast extract like Marmite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yeast extract' looks like one ingredient; 'extract' is the definition. Cook rearranges IN, WOK, LUE and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To winkle out is to extract something with difficulty, like a winkle from its shell.

clue.text: Vitamin — hermit swallows it up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole is read from bottom to top
swallows means the hermit word takes in the word it

parts.note: a hermit is a loner, someone who lives apart

explanation.surface: A recluse gulps down a vitamin pill.
explanation.walkthrough: One reversal turns the whole hermit-with-it word, not just the inserted part.
explanation.definitionFit: Retinol is the chemical name for vitamin A, used in skin creams.

clue.text: A degree sound to approach in reverse gear with a truck?

indicators.note: sound tells us the phrase is spoken, its sound giving a different spelling

parts.words: to approach in reverse gear with a truck
parts.note: to back a lorry at something is to approach it reversing in a truck; lorry is British for truck

explanation.surface: A qualification in reversing a truck up to something, as if for an HGV test.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'back a lorry at' runs together into the name of the degree. Lorry is the British word for a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: A baccalaureate is a bachelor's degree, or the International Baccalaureate school qualification.

clue.text: Wilder game that includes everyone's personal information

parts.note: Gene Wilder was the American comic actor of Willy Wonka fame
pool is a cue game played on a table

explanation.surface: A game played by the actor Wilder holds secrets about everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: POOL is the billiards-style table game.
explanation.definitionFit: A gene pool is the total genetic material of a population, the personal code of all its members.

clue.text: Order small fish, consuming a bird with it

indicators.note: consuming means the fish word eats the other pieces

parts.note: fry are young, small fish
a tern is a seabird
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone orders tiny fish which go on to eat a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a brotherhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraternity is a brotherhood or religious order of men united by a shared purpose.

clue.text: Some think it's chintzy

indicators.note: some of means only a part of the words is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A view of a fabric's showiness that not everybody shares.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in it's is ignored; the whole clue also describes the answer, since some people think chintz tasteless.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch is gaudy, sentimental taste, much like cheap flowery chintz fabric.

clue.text: Action of baby, naked, to hug clothes

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the hug word dresses the naked word, going round it

parts.note: to cling is to hold tightly, to hug
raw means bare or naked, as in in the raw

explanation.surface: A naked baby clutching at clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' reads as a noun, but it is the verb: one piece dresses, or surrounds, the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Crawling on hands and knees is how a baby moves before walking.

clue.text: Bovine out of oxygen, smile playing on the face of it

indicators.note: playing means the letters are moved around
out of means the bovine word is removed from oxygen

parts.note: an ox is a bovine animal

explanation.surface: A cow, deprived of air, still seems to smile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' takes OX from OXYGEN, leaving YGEN; 'playing' then rearranges YGEN with SMILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemingly means apparently, judging by how things look at first sight.

clue.text: Pet food ending on menu in African city

parts.note: mog is British slang for a pet cat
a dish is a serving of food

indicators.note: ending on means the last letter of menu is taken

explanation.surface: Cat food is the final item on a menu in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: MOG (or moggy) is everyday British for a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mogadishu is the capital of Somalia, on the Horn of Africa coast.

clue.text: See 9
Heartless, release bricks

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the release phrase is removed

parts.note: to let go is to release

explanation.surface: A callous order to drop the bricks.
explanation.walkthrough: LET GO loses its middle letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Lego is the Danish brand of interlocking plastic toy bricks.

clue.text: German mathematician has written up note that is carried by the Queen to her friends?

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the queen word

parts.note: close friends might call Queen Elizabeth Liz

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: NB, nota bene, is a written note to take notice
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A German mathematician jots a note that the Queen's friends pass round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' turns both short abbreviations together before they go inside the friendly name for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Leibniz was the German polymath who devised calculus alongside Newton.

clue.text: Like to eat something for a baby, like stew

indicators.note: to eat means the like word swallows the next pieces

parts.note: such means like this or of that kind
a cot is a baby's bed
as means like, in the same way

explanation.surface: Something resembling a baby's food, rather like a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: A cot is the British word for a crib; 'Like' appears twice with two different jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Succotash is an American stew of sweetcorn and lima beans.

clue.text: Revolutionary deal negotiated in English town

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

indicators.note: negotiated means the letters of deal are worked round

explanation.surface: A rebel strikes a bargain in a town in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheadle is a town near Stockport in Greater Manchester, with another in Staffordshire.

clue.text: Hot butt, he kissed Beth madly in illicit extra-curricular activity

parts.note: smoking can mean very hot, as smoking hot
the behind is the butt or bottom

indicators.note: madly means the letters are rearranged wildly

explanation.surface: A passionate schoolboy snogs Beth behind the school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot butt' looks like a lit cigarette end, apt to the answer, but it is two separate synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret cigarettes behind the bicycle shelter are the classic British schoolchild's forbidden pastime.

clue.text: See 19
Elevated freezer?

definitions.meaning: as in a ... view, seen from high above
... is a British brand of frozen food

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the freezer as a brand found in it, not a description.
explanation.definitionFit: A view from high above is a bird's-eye view, and Birds Eye makes frozen fish fingers.

clue.text: Brilliantly creative mind, however David Miliband is off?

parts.note: if David Miliband is off, his brother ..., the pair having fought for the Labour leadership in 2010

explanation.surface: A political observer says a clever brain survives even if one Miliband goes.
explanation.walkthrough: David and Ed Miliband are brothers who both stood for the British Labour Party leadership; with David out, ED IS ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison, inventor of the phonograph and light bulb, is a byword for creative genius.

clue.text: Drive that's 1,760 yards up the hill, all may conclude

parts.note: 1,760 yards is one mile, written 1m and read as IM

indicators.note: all may conclude means each word gives its final letter

explanation.surface: A drive of a mile up a hill at the end of a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 in 1m is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone forward to act.

clue.text: Impromptu is sustained without soprano solo

indicators.note: something impromptu is improvised, so these letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: An improvised piece is held without a soprano's solo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means with outside: S joins SUSTAINED and the whole is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo effort is done without help, by oneself alone.

clue.text: 2 — 1 to enter score, of course

indicators.note: to enter means the 1 goes into the score word

parts.note: par is the standard score on a golf course
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A golfer's scorecard, number one going in at two.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a set of two things, like a pair of socks.

clue.text: University in the area shortly needing detective — gadzooks!

indicators.note: in means the university letter sits inside the area word
shortly means the area word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a zone is an area
DS is a detective sergeant

explanation.surface: A university district briefly calls in a detective, to cries of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Zounds and gadzooks are both archaic oaths of surprise, minced forms of God's wounds and God's hooks.

clue.text: Hire car for Spooner causing tiredness

indicators.note: Spooner swaps the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: to let a property is to hire it out
a Jag is a Jaguar car

explanation.surface: A rented car leaves the driver exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Jet lag is fatigue after crossing time zones on a long flight.
